guide: This setup shows you how people use your app and alerts you when it breaks, using PostHog for behaviour and Sentry for errors. You need a working web app, a free PostHog account and a free Sentry account.
1. Create a PostHog project and copy its project API key from the project settings.
1. Install the PostHog JavaScript library in your web app and initialise it once at start-up with that key.
1. Turn on session recordings in PostHog so you can watch real visits and see where people get stuck.
1. Add custom events for the actions that matter, such as signing up or finishing a key task, so you can see how people use each feature.
1. Create a Sentry project for your framework and install its SDK, using the DSN (the project's address) it gives you.
1. Initialise Sentry at start-up, then trigger a deliberate test error to confirm it appears in your Sentry dashboard.
1. Deploy to Vercel (or your host), adding both keys as environment variables there, and set Sentry to email you on new errors.
1. Each week, watch a few PostHog recordings and read new Sentry issues, then fix the biggest problem first.
Watch out: Never commit your keys to the code or send personal details such as names or emails as event data. Add them as environment variables and only send what you need.

```
You are helping me add product analytics and error tracking to my existing web app. Build it step by step and explain each change briefly.
My stack: <framework, for example Next.js or React>. I host on <Vercel or other host>. I have free accounts with PostHog and Sentry.
Do the following:
1. Install and initialise the PostHog JavaScript SDK using an environment variable for the project API key. Enable session recordings.
2. Add custom event tracking for these actions: <list 3 to 5 key actions, for example sign up, create profile, share link>.
3. Install and initialise the Sentry SDK for my framework using an environment variable for the DSN. Add a temporary test button that throws an error so I can confirm it reaches Sentry.
4. Do not include any personal data such as names, emails or exact locations in events or error reports. Mask text inputs in recordings.
5. Keep all keys out of the code and list the environment variables I need to add to my host and to a local env file.
Return the changed files, the exact install commands, the environment variables to set, and a short checklist for testing that both tools are receiving data before I deploy.
```
